module_mood_contract: A compact orientation map, a deliberate early encounter with the training-wide model, not a spent reveal: the engineer sees a path they are already on, understands why each gain in reach exposes the next constraint, and leaves ambitious but calibrated about the rest of AE101.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the rule guards against: a closer-shaped 'here's the pattern you just lived' framing landing before the student has lived anything, so it reads as abstract claim instead of recognition. Not present here - this file is a ceiling-showing orientation map ('Demo lectures showing a ceiling go at beginning' per the rule's own diagnostic), not a naming-what-you-just-did closer. It is placed at the M1->M2 gap (open) and reappears at M4 Prework as an explicit 'forward-look' (line 12, run-the-first-experiment.md), both pre-experience positions. Strategy doc content-strategy-agentic-engineering-101.md line 297 independently frames it the same way: 'a deliberate early encounter with the training-wide model, not a spent reveal.'

Rule targets pre-exercise lectures gating an M5-style contrast-mood module, where over-teaching collapses the felt-evidence the closer depends on. This file is optional supplementary reading (not a mandatory pre-exercise lecture) linked before M2 (plan-mode teaching mood, not contrast-mood) and, per its own maintainer block, as an 'optional forward look' before M4 (testing/curious-readiness mood). It never sits directly in front of M5's contrast exercise as a gating lecture, so the harm this rule prevents has no surface to land on here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No cross-module sequencing in lecture bodies.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: module numbering in shared-library body text ties a re-placeable file to one sequence position. Ran `sed -n '1,103p' agentic-engineering-progression.md | grep -n "M[0-9]"` against the body above the maintainer fence (lines 1-102) - zero matches. No M1/M2/M4/M5 references appear in student-facing prose; all module-placement claims live in the maintainer block below the fence, which is the correct location.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide/lecture headers pass the squint test AND the truth clause.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: an empty-container or orphan-mystery header that names nothing, or a header the body doesn't support. Headers here (Assistance / Interactive work / Delegating bounded outcomes / Directing parallel sessions / Encoding checked loops / Improving the system / Part 1: The progression / Part 2: The leverage model / One model, not two) each name a concept or the section's one claim; none are empty-container shapes ('The move', 'The question') or orphan mystery. No header duplication. 'One model, not two' is a claim header and the body directly supports it (Part 1's per-level constraints ARE the same calibration-licenses-reach mechanism as Part 2's diagram).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slide's BODY is size-bounded (~210 words, <=6 bullets), not just its header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a slide too dense to stay glance-legible when projected. Ran a word count per ## section excluding the inline SVG figure block (per the rule's own exclusion): largest sections are 'Part 2: The leverage model' at 163 words and 'Interactive work' / 'Part 1: The progression' at 83 words - all comfortably under 210. No section carries more than 4 bullets (Part 2's four reach/calibration bullets is the densest list in the file).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Classroom = default delivery; body teaches work, trainer manages room.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: authored conversation/pause cues ('discuss with your neighbor', 'take 90 seconds and compare') that script the trainer's room-management into student-facing text. Grepped the body for discuss/compare/share/tell-the-room/pause shapes - none present. Every sentence is about the work (the level's practice, the diagram's axes, the model), never cohort pacing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a body paragraph narrating a forcing function that should instead be enacted by a prompt the student copies. This file is a prework/prep-read supplementary with no exercise phases and no student-copied prompts anywhere in it - there is no forcing function to misplace, so the rule has no surface here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named (mood-floor 8+/10 per beat on teaching beats, mood-exempt on setup beats).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a beat scored below the 8+ floor while claiming to teach, or a mechanical setup beat wrongly held to that floor. This whole file is a teaching beat (no setup/launch mechanics), so the floor applies throughout. Regenerated the Class A persona trace against current content (previous cache was stale - content_sha mismatch, since the file grew substantially from a bare six-line list to full per-level bodies in commit a737e54, after the cached trace and after the 0774e2f audit stamp). New trace: phase mood_score 8, close mood_score 8, both at floor - the expanded level bodies plus the per-level 'Moves you up:' constraint give the persona concrete recognition of their own practice without turning session-count into a score.

Harm: the page's uncertainty reading as 'I did something wrong' rather than 'I don't yet know'. Body language throughout is descriptive-causal ('moves you up', 'exposes the constraint') with no shame register; Reckless autonomy is drawn as a named trap-state on the diagram, not addressed at the reader as a personal failure.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a title/Big-Idea built around a failure word rather than the discipline it protects. Every level is named for the positive practice (Assistance, Delegating bounded outcomes, Encoding checked loops); 'Reckless autonomy' appears only as one of four diagram quadrant labels illustrating the failure case the discipline (calibrated agency) addresses, never as the page's own framing or title.

Confirmed the diagram is byte-identical to its canonical parent, curriculum/lectures/the-gate-is-a-claim.md (same viewBox, aria-label, axis labels, quadrant text, frontier caption), satisfying the maintainer block's 'keep the model and labels synchronized' instruction. Module-to-module arc and Big Idea fidelity both hold: this is a sanctioned, strategy-authored repetition, not an unplanned spoiler.
